headline: Nothing live yet. Paper forward test running.
spoken: Evening. Here's your Quint roundup for Thursday 19 November.
Real money: no bot is trading a real or prop account yet, so nothing has been made or lost.
Paper forward test: nine bots are on paper since Wednesday 18 November. No trades yet, because no new candles have come in since their rules were fixed.
Best backtest so far: the 20-candle breakout, $3,711 over 40 trades on one MNQ. That is too few trades to trust yet.
No strategy has earned approval yet. That needs years of data and a clean paper test.
Warning: four bots would likely fail a Lucid 50K before passing: New York open breakout, Opening candle direction (5-minute opening range), Last-30-minute momentum, Failed breakout.

Latest lesson: Replaying WYLD's rules exactly as the indicator reads them showed where setups die: the pools marked before the open were all run before 9:30, most sweeps found no higher-timeframe level holding nearby, and on 5-minute candles Point B came before any confirmation.

Next up: Grow the MNQ candle store every night with one TradingView call: the newest 1-minute candles (from 19 Nov 2026), merged into lab/data; the 5- and 15-minute candles are built from them after an exact match check against the stored ones (5-minute candles are fetched instead if they ever differ or leave a gap).

strategies.name: Your strategy: WYLD Will Four Pillars
strategies.timeframe: 1m entries, 15m liquidity, monthly to daily levels
strategies.verdict: Your main strategy, and WYLD Will's rules are the master. Not backtested as WYLD states it yet: a few rules aren't exact (the easiest equal highs and lows, the stop buffer, the break-even trigger, entries per PDR). The two coded versions in your apps are older and stricter than WYLD (Chart Wizard's took 0 trades in 4 weeks), so they should be brought in line with WYLD's rules. His results are his own claims.

strategies.name: 20-candle breakout
strategies.verdict: Beat its costs on 11 weeks of MNQ, but lost money in the first half and made it all in the October to November sell-off, mostly on shorts. One day was 45% of the profit. Promising, not proven.

strategies.name: New York open breakout
strategies.verdict: Just over break-even, and only because of one big day. Without that day it lost money. The weakest case for staying in the app.

strategies.name: Opening candle direction (5-minute opening range)
strategies.verdict: First read only: 20 trades.

strategies.name: Last-30-minute momentum
strategies.verdict: Strong academic evidence over decades, but it lost on the 4 weeks we have. One trade a day, so it needs years to judge.

strategies.name: VWAP trend
strategies.verdict: Needs 1-minute candles, which the lab doesn't have. Trades often, so check Lucid's microscalping rule.

strategies.name: Gap fade
strategies.verdict: Lowest priority. Its published drawdown is bigger than a 50K's max loss.

strategies.name: Inverted fair value gap
strategies.verdict: First read only: 12 trades.

strategies.name: Range squeeze breakout
strategies.verdict: Needs 1-minute candles.

strategies.name: Trend-join scalper
strategies.verdict: Needs about 80% winners just to break even. Needs 1-minute candles.

strategies.name: VWAP band fade
strategies.verdict: Best-looking first read (30 trades), which is still an anecdote.

strategies.name: Failed breakout
strategies.verdict: Lost on the first read (9 trades).

strategies.name: Noise-area momentum
strategies.verdict: The strongest outside evidence of anything here, and the only family the factory let through on its first night (6 survivors, PBO 29%). Still weeks of data, a falling market, and samples just over 30 trades. Drawdowns can last over a year.

strategies.name: RSI(2) all-weather (saved on TraderDev as '[retest] QQQ COMBO RSI2 all-weather 1h')
strategies.verdict: Rejected as it stands: on real MNQ it lost money, its worst drawdown was 2.5 times Lucid's max loss, and it has no stop loss. The long side alone made a little, which is a new idea to test on untouched data, not a result.

strategies.name: Prop B: RSI(2) combo, Globex day, flat by 4pm New York (TraderDev)
strategies.verdict: Looks positive on the QQQ stand-in only. Its close cousin lost on real MNQ, so expect the same until it's tested there.

strategies.name: Prop A: EMA + ATR trailing stop, long only, Globex day, flat by 4pm New York (TraderDev)
strategies.verdict: Small edge on the stand-in. The plan's walk-forward evidence says ATR trailing trend lost on MNQ hourly (PF 0.49).

strategies.name: Prop A and B, regular-hours-only versions on 5m and 15m (TraderDev, 3 strategies)
strategies.verdict: Rejected: during the hours that matter for a day trader these had no edge or lost, even on the flattering stand-in (RSI2 5m about $1 a trade over 217 trades; EMA-ATR 5m -$2,836; EMA-ATR 15m -$2,542; rough 1-MNQ figures).

strategies.name: Prop B: RSI(2) combo, regular hours only, 15m (TraderDev)
strategies.verdict: The only regular-hours version that stayed positive on the stand-in, and only just. Unproven: its cousin lost on real MNQ.

strategies.name: Other TraderDev retests: Bollinger squeeze 15m, Bollinger mean-reversion long 15m, EMA ATR trail long 1h, pivot break + volume 1h, trend pullback EMA96/EMA50 15m
strategies.verdict: All look positive once TraderDev's crypto fees are swapped for MNQ costs (rough: squeeze +$9,677, mean-reversion +$7,078, EMA ATR +$5,728, pivot +$2,707, trend pullback +$12,408), but only on the QQQ stand-in, whose overnight hours are thin. The plan's walk-forward test found EMA pullback and ATR trailing trend lost on real MNQ. Unproven.

strategies.name: Lucid MNQ sweep + volume (TraderDev)
strategies.verdict: Rejected for now: 16 trades in six months and about break-even before costs. Liquidity-grab signals also failed the 947-day MNQ study. Version 1 can't run on TraderDev (it uses strategy.closedtrades.profit).

strategies.name: RSI(2) pullback, daily
strategies.verdict: Holds overnight, so only where the account allows it (research/prop-firms/OVERNIGHT-FUTURES.md).

strategies.name: Long-term trend following
strategies.verdict: Deep drawdowns that trailing-drawdown prop accounts punish. A personal-account idea for later.

lessons.lesson: Replaying WYLD's rules exactly as the indicator reads them showed where setups die: the pools marked before the open were all run before 9:30, most sweeps found no higher-timeframe level holding nearby, and on 5-minute candles Point B came before any confirmation. A pillar can only be judged with the data it was designed for: 1-minute candles for the confirmation, and an exact rule for which pools count.

Testing thousands of variations finds lucky winners easily: on the first night breakout and opening range scored PBO 60 to 67%, meaning their best variations were mostly luck. Only judge on unseen sessions, PBO, neighbours and the Lucid gate.

The owner's strategy is WYLD Will's Four Pillars, the master version. Trading Mastery's six steps and Chart Wizard's 5 pillars are older codings of it, not separate strategies. Keep one entry and one checklist.
